summary: Merops (Ancient Greek Μέροψ) of Percote was a seer who foresaw the deaths of his sons Amphius (Araphius) and Adrastus in the Trojan War; they ignored him and were slain by Diomedes. He was also father of Cleite (wife of Cyzicus) and Arisbe (first wife of Priam), and taught Aesacus to interpret dreams.
etymology: Ancient Greek Μέροψ (Mérops), "mankind," "mortals," or "dividing the voice."

sections.heading: Seer of Percote
paragraphs: Homer calls Merops above all men skilled in prophecy. He forbade his sons to join the war; black fate led them on, and Diomedes killed both. Apollodorus and the Epic Cycle keep the same Percotean house.
Through Arisbe he touches Priam's early marriage; through Cleite he links to the Argonauts' Dolione tragedy at Cyzicus. He also instructed Aesacus in dream-interpretation.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Other Meropes include the Ethiopian king husband of Clymene (adoptive father of Phaethon — atlas merops-ethiopia), a Coan king turned into the constellation Aquila, and minor fathers in Milesian and Heraclid stemmata. The atlas id merops-percote is the Percotean seer alone.
